Subject: Behavioral delta after model swap — immediate attention requested

Hi Rishi / Laura,

We're seeing a marked change in behavior after the model swap you performed on 2026-12-02 (vX.3 -> vX.4 with new int8 profile). Over the last 3 hours our p95 has gone from ~120ms to ~340ms and p99 is intermittently above 900ms. Separately, our automated sampling shows increased hallucination rate on safety-critical prompts (samples attached).

Impact:
- Latency: p95 up 3x, p99 spikes causing client timeouts (seen ~0.8% 502s).
- Quality: 4% increase in classification mislabel on our test harness (attached).
- Throughput: effective RPS capacity has dropped ~30% during peak.

We've attached a perf snapshot and a trace file. We have an upcoming investor demo tomorrow and need a short-term mitigation plan (rollback or variant pinning) plus a timeline for full root-cause. Please advise next steps and confirm a point of contact for 1:1 coordination.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Head of AI Infrastructure
SolventAI

Sanjay — thanks for the fast heads-up and the traces. I'm standing this up as a priority incident.

Two immediate asks from my side:
1) Can you confirm whether you routed any traffic to the vX.4 int8-optimized variant only, or whether both int8 and fp16 variants were in the pool?
2) If you have one or two sample prompts that reproduce the hallucination behavior reliably, please send them (we already have your attached sample set but reproducible prompts help a lot).

What we'll do now:
- I'll open an internal troubleshooting thread with runtime and model-onboarding (cc'ing Laura + Marissa).
- If the data points show quantization-related decode stalls or kernel fallbacks, we will recommend an emergency pin to the previous variant (vX.3) for a safe window while we triage.
- I'll also propose a 30-minute leadership sync tomorrow morning (PST) to confirm rollback/communication strategy for your investor demo.

I'll be your direct point of contact for coordination. Expect an internal update within 45 minutes.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra

Marissa / Laura — forwarding SolventAI's escalation (below). Key points from initial triage:

Summary (so far):
- Customer: SolventAI, high-value strategic account (D-73421).
- Trigger: Deployment of model vX.4 with an int8 quantization profile on 2026-12-02; customer reports 3x p95, p99 spikes, and increased hallucinations.
- Customer impact: investor demo scheduled tomorrow; they are observing production timeouts and quality degradation.
- Attachments: perf_snapshot_2026-12-03.json, p99_trace.txt (they shared).

What runtime/infra have observed (preliminary):
- Several decode threads show kernel fallback events when sequence length > 512; these correlate with the p99 spikes in the trace.
- Batch sizes increased unexpectedly for a subset of traffic (likely due to new batching heuristics interacting with token distribution), causing queuing amplification.
- No OOMs; GPU utilization modestly higher but latency distribution changed.

Suggested immediate actions (recommendation for leadership):
1) Emergency pin the customer to vX.3 (fp16) for a 4-hour window to stabilize latencies and remove quality risk. We can do a targeted variant pin without full rollback.
2) Temporarily disable the new batching heuristics for their pool to prevent queuing amplification while we analyze token distribution.
3) Execute a quick smoke validation on vX.4 int8 with synthetic safety prompts to reproduce hallucination pattern; if reproduced, isolate quantization path.

Risk/Tradeoffs:
- Pinning to vX.3 reduces the customer's short-term cost savings and the engineering data we were hoping to collect on int8 at scale.
- Not pinning risks customer churn and an executive escalation given the demo timeline.

Request: Marissa, can you join a 30-min leadership huddle today at 11:30 PST to decide whether to authorize emergency pin + customer communication? Laura, can you confirm infra has an automated variant-pin flow we can trigger per-account?

I'll prepare a 1-page incident brief and synthetic reproducer by 10:30 PST. Attaching the customer's perf snapshot and a short internal trace excerpt.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
